To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spatial skills are important for the operation of robots in industry, and that spatial training can be implemented through robotics education.

(1) spatial skills are essential for operating and programming robotic manipulators; (2) novice engineering students have a poor understanding of spatial skills and their role in robot manipulation; (3) the proposed learning practices in robotics laboratory can improve spatial skills; (4) the proposed learning practice can be applied to both high school and undergraduate students.
the spatial skills required for programming and operating robots can be trained by means of robotics laboratory classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to spatial skills development in robotics education, which is a significant step in the process of engineering education innovation at the Technion.
the development of spatial abilities in engineering education.
the question of how the spatial abilities of students can be improved through robotics education, and how the robotics laboratory can be designed for this purpose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial skills of the participants in the workshop have improved.
the proposed practice can be a valuable addition to engineering education.
spatial skills training is an important component in the education of engineering students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spatial training is a key factor to enhance students’ performance and interest in learning robotics and automation technologies.
the spatial training of novice engineering students through robotics is feasible and effective.
we found that the proposed learning practice is effective for spatial skill development of novice learners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robotics workshop can be an effective tool to enhance the spatial skills of novice engineering students, especially those who have no previous experience in robotics.
robotics can serve as an educational tool to develop spatial skills of novice engineering students.
the spatial skills required for robot manipulation are not innate, and can be developed by learning practices in robotics.
